title: Warning/error squiggles don't render for the last line in a file
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in v4.8.dev.custom_build [4e244f211] ### System information Godot v4.8.dev (4e244f211) - macOS Unknown (27.0.0) - Multi-window, 2 monitors (4608x2592 @ 120.00 Hz, 3840x2160 @ 60.00 Hz) - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Apple M4 Pro - Apple M4 Pro (14 threads) - 24.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description If the last line of a GDScript file has a warning that encompasses its whole range (such as an untyped declaration for a class property), the warning squiggles will not render. With an empty newline following the last line of the file (how it should look): When the line with the warning is the last line in the file: Adding a comment to the end of the line, thus making the end of the warning's range not be the end of the file itself, allows the squiggle to display: Note that hovering over the line still shows diagnostic information (i.e., the warning message), so it is indeed related to the squiggle-rendering code specifically. ### Steps to reproduce Create a GDScript file. On the last line of the file, declare a variable/property without specifying its type, so that the line emits the `UNTYPED_DECLARATION` warning. Do not save the file as the editor may automatically add an empty newline and thus cause the squiggle to display. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A
